policy: Universe V7.2 inheritance + daughter-specific sources; continuous monitoring; new generic parent gaps route to Universe V7.3 queue.

sources.title: Process Classification Framework
sources.supports: Enterprise process crosswalks.
sources.notSupports: Does not prescribe mode-specific ocean execution.

sources.title: Bills of Lading / Charter Party Clauses and Contracts
sources.supports: Maritime contractual clauses and carriage-document context.
sources.notSupports: Not a universal public process standard; contract wording and governing law control.

sources.title: IMO/ILO/UNECE Code of Practice for Packing of Cargo Transport Units
sources.version: 2014 published baseline · 2025 revision under 2026 finalization/endorsement; not promoted
sources.supports: Packing, securing, handling, information flow and unpacking of cargo transport units across sea/land/intermodal chains.
sources.notSupports: Non-mandatory global code; 2025 revision must not replace the 2014 baseline until formal endorsement/publication is clear.
sources.changeWatch: CTU Code 2025 revision · ECE/TRANS/WP.24/2026/8 · finalization in progress, not promoted.

sources.title: Arrival Notice Standard
sources.supports: Structured carrier arrival notice creation, updates and distribution.
sources.notSupports: Local notice requirements and cargo-release legal effects may differ.

sources.title: Industry Blueprint
sources.supports: Container-shipping business-process reference across Shipment, Equipment and Vessel journeys.
sources.notSupports: DCSA scope is container shipping; it does not define LCL forwarder/CFS house-layer execution end-to-end.

sources.title: Booking Standard
sources.supports: Carrier-customer booking lifecycle/data including request, confirmation, amendment/cancellation and special-cargo data.
sources.notSupports: Does not define all internal carrier decisions or LCL house-booking workflows.

sources.title: Commercial Schedules Standard
sources.supports: Point-to-point routing, port schedules and vessel schedules exchanged by carriers.
sources.notSupports: Schedule information is not booking confirmation or legal carriage commitment.

sources.title: Bill of Lading / eBL Standard
sources.supports: Shipping Instructions and Transport Document lifecycle; issuance, surrender and endorsement modules within DCSA scope.
sources.notSupports: Legal effect still depends on applicable substantive law and document/contract.

sources.title: Port Call Standard
sources.version: 2.0 · current 2.0 family at Universe V7 snapshot
sources.supports: Operational port-call information exchange among carriers, terminals, ports and service providers.
sources.notSupports: Cargo-operation official instructions remain separate processes where outside standard scope.

sources.title: Track & Trace Standard
sources.supports: Container shipment event semantics across pre-shipment, pre-ocean, ocean, post-ocean and post-shipment phases.
sources.notSupports: Does not create legal custody or liability rules by itself.
sources.changeWatch: DCSA 2026 roadmap indicates Track & Trace 3.0 development; 2.2 remains current implementable standard at this snapshot.

sources.title: Verified Gross Mass Standard
sources.supports: Digital VGM declaration exchange.
sources.notSupports: Does not replace SOLAS shipper responsibility or national weighing-method rules.

sources.title: FIATA freight-forwarding definition, documents and resources
sources.supports: Freight-forwarder instruments including FCR, FCT, FWR, FBL/FWB and guidance.
sources.notSupports: Does not prescribe one global LCL CFS workflow or supersede national law.

sources.title: Practical Guide to the Electronic FIATA Multimodal Bill of Lading (eFBL)
sources.supports: Digital FBL issuance/traceability for FIATA freight forwarders/MTOs.
sources.notSupports: A FIATA FBL is not equivalent to every house B/L used in market practice.

sources.title: Ocean Transportation Intermediary / NVOCC regulatory definitions
sources.version: Shipping Act / 46 CFR Part 515 context · current FMC guidance
sources.supports: U.S.-trade OTI/OFF/NVOCC role, licensing and regulatory context; NVOCC issues its own house B/L/equivalent and is shipper to the vessel-operating common carrier.
sources.notSupports: Must not be generalized into a global NVOCC legal definition or universal liability rule.

sources.title: International Maritime Dangerous Goods Code
sources.supports: Packaged dangerous-goods maritime requirements.
sources.notSupports: National/port/flag implementation and carrier restrictions still require context.

sources.title: IMO Compendium on Facilitation and Electronic Business
sources.supports: Harmonized maritime data semantics for ships, ports, MSWs and authorities.
sources.notSupports: Not a complete shipment execution workflow.

sources.title: International Convention for Safe Containers
sources.supports: Container structural safety and international safety regime.
sources.notSupports: Does not define container booking or documentation workflow.

sources.title: Convention on Facilitation of International Maritime Traffic (FAL)
sources.version: As amended; MSW mandatory since 1 Jan 2024
sources.supports: Ship/port reporting and Maritime Single Window obligation.
sources.notSupports: Does not define private carrier commercial booking or freight-forwarder operations.

sources.title: ISO 17712 — Freight containers — Mechanical seals
sources.supports: Mechanical freight-container seal classification and acceptance.
sources.notSupports: Seal process/accountability controls require operating procedures and security context.

sources.title: ISO 6346 — Freight containers — Coding, identification and marking
sources.supports: Container identification, size/type coding and marks.
sources.notSupports: Does not cover all safety/regulatory marks; Edition 5 is under publication.
sources.changeWatch: Edition 5 is under publication in Aug 2026; do not silently replace 2022 until published.

sources.title: Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records
sources.supports: Legal framework principles for electronic transferable records such as bills of lading.
sources.notSupports: Does not itself apply unless enacted/influential law; does not change substantive carriage law.

sources.title: United Nations Convention on Negotiable Cargo Documents (Accra Convention)
sources.version: Adopted 15 Dec 2025 · not yet in force at 29 Aug 2026
sources.supports: Future harmonized legal framework for negotiable cargo documents in paper/electronic form across modes.
sources.notSupports: Not yet in force; must not be treated as an active carriage/document legal requirement.
sources.changeWatch: Convention is adopted but not yet in force and opens for signature in Accra on 26 Oct 2026; keep legal applicability conditional.

sources.title: SCOR Digital Standard
sources.supports: Enterprise supply-chain process architecture and directional crosswalks.
sources.notSupports: Does not prescribe ocean booking, terminal, vessel, CFS, document or legal workflows.

sources.title: Recommended stable terminal / ship-planning message guides
sources.version: BAPLIE 3.1.1 (D.13B) recommended stable; MOVINS 2.1.2 maintained stable; COPRAR/COARRI/COPARN/CODECO 2.1.3 (D.00B) recommended stable
sources.supports: Terminal/carrier EDI exchange semantics for ship planning, vessel load/discharge orders/confirmations, terminal booking and gate events where adopted.
sources.notSupports: Does not establish a universal terminal business-process sequence or prove adoption by a specific carrier/terminal.
sources.changeWatch: Re-check maintained/recommended SMDG message-guide versions and implementation adoption at each source review.

sources.title: SOLAS VI/2 + VGM Guidelines
sources.supports: Mandatory VGM responsibility and loading precondition for packed containers.
sources.notSupports: Does not define carrier API implementation.

sources.title: TIC4.0 semantics, dataset, data model and definitions
sources.supports: Terminal process semantics and data definitions.
sources.notSupports: Adoption-specific; not a legal rule or complete carrier process.

sources.title: Cross-Border Management Reference Data Model
sources.supports: Cross-border regulatory data alignment across transport/trade/customs.
sources.notSupports: Does not replace national customs law or competent-authority procedure.

sources.title: International Forwarding and Transport BRS · Overall v2
sources.supports: High-level syntax-neutral forwarding and multimodal transport process/message-exchange requirements; detailed subset BRSs govern implementation detail.
sources.notSupports: Does not prescribe one local CFS operating sequence, terminal implementation, or carrier-specific workflow.

sources.title: Visibility and Collaborative Planning in Multimodal Supply Chain Operations BRS
sources.supports: Generic cross-modal Transport Event Registry semantics and governed access/delegation for operational visibility and collaboration across multimodal logistics actors.
sources.notSupports: Does not replace DCSA/GS1/mode-specific execution standards, prove platform adoption, or prescribe one universal end-to-end execution sequence.

sources.title: UN/CEFACT Reference Data Models — Multi-Modal Transport / Buy-Ship-Pay transport semantics
sources.version: MMT RDM + current D25A transport views · 11 Jun 2026
sources.supports: Shared transport, consignment, document and multimodal data semantics.
sources.notSupports: Does not prescribe one universal carrier/forwarder operating sequence.

sources.title: WCO Data Model
sources.supports: Customs data interoperability and information packages.
sources.notSupports: Does not define national declaration procedure or carrier commercial workflow.

sources.title: Trade Facilitation Agreement
sources.supports: High-level customs release/clearance, pre-arrival processing, transit and border cooperation obligations.
sources.notSupports: National implementation details remain jurisdiction-specific.
